A.claim: A holder of a project's read-only API key can delete that project's checks, because the delete view is wrapped by the decorator that accepts read-only keys and never checks the read-only flag.

An API key for one project can list the checks of every other project with the same owner, including ping and update URLs with a read-write key, because the list query filters by project owner instead of by the key's project.
A read-only key can obtain a check's uuid, ping URL and management URLs by looking the check up by unique_key, because that view builds the response without passing the read-only flag.
A foreign website could make cross-origin requests to key-authenticated API endpoints because they send Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *.
A caller can supply the API key in the JSON request body instead of the header, which might bypass header-based key checks.
A caller could authenticate by submitting a stored key hash as a plain-text key, because the legacy plain-text lookup branch could match the hashed value stored in the key column.
A key could resolve to the wrong project because the hashed-key lookup selects candidate projects by an 8-character prefix.
A caller could gain or lose privileges because whether a request is read-only is derived from the hcr_ prefix of the presented key.
A key could read the status-change history of another project's check because the flips-by-uuid view fetches the check by uuid without a project filter.
A key could read another project's check or its status changes through the unique_key lookup views because they might not be scoped to the key's project.
A read-write key could attach another project's notification channels to its checks during create or update because channel lookup might not be scoped to the project.
A key could update, pause, resume or read pings and ping bodies of another project's check because those views might not compare the check's project with the key's project.
An attacker could brute-force API keys because wrong keys are not rate limited.
A key holder can learn whether a check uuid exists in another project because the lookup returns 404 for unknown uuids and 403 for foreign ones.
A caller could recover the metrics key through a timing side channel because the metrics endpoint compares the X-Metrics-Key header with a plain inequality.
Unauthenticated callback endpoints and slug-based check auto-provisioning may let unauthenticated callers act on checks.
The Prometheus integration endpoint may expose project check data under a separate authentication scheme that was not reviewed.
Legacy 32-character plain-text API keys are still accepted, which keeps weaker, unhashed keys usable.

B.claim: A holder of a project's read-only API key can delete that project's checks, because the delete view uses the decorator that accepts read-only keys and never checks the read-only flag.

An API key for one project can list the checks of every other project with the same owner, including uuids and ping URLs with a read-write key, because the list query filters by project owner instead of by the key's project.
A read-only key placed in a POST body could be accepted where only the read-write key should be.
A read-only key could create, update, pause or resume checks.
A key could read or change another project's single check by uuid (get, update, delete, pause, resume, pings, ping body, flips).
A key could reach another project's checks through the unique_key lookup, unique_key flips or badges views.
A key could resolve to the wrong project, or a read-only key could match the read-write column, because the hashed-key lookup selects candidates by an 8-character prefix.
Two projects sharing the same legacy plain-text key could make the key lookup raise MultipleObjectsReturned, because the api_key column has no uniqueness constraint.
Read-only keys are refused on the channels, pings and ping body endpoints, which is stricter than the other read endpoints.
An attacker could guess API keys because there is no rate limit on key attempts, which matters for any low-entropy legacy keys.
A foreign website could make cross-origin API requests because the API sends Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *.

C.claim: A holder of a project's read-only API key can delete that project's checks, because the delete view uses the decorator that accepts read-only keys and never checks the read-only flag.

An API key for one project can list the checks of every other project with the same owner, including ping, update, pause and resume URLs with a read-write key, because the list query filters by project owner instead of by the key's project.
A read-only key can obtain a check's uuid, ping URL and management URLs by looking the check up by unique_key, because that view builds the response without passing the read-only flag.
An attacker could recover legacy plain-text keys through timing because the plain-text key lookup is not a constant-time comparison.
A key holder can learn whether a check uuid exists in another project because the lookup returns 404 for unknown uuids and 403 for foreign ones.
A caller can supply the API key in the JSON request body instead of the header.
A read-only key could be accepted by endpoints that require the read-write key.

D.claim: A holder of a project's read-only API key can delete that project's checks, because the delete view uses the decorator that accepts read-only keys and never checks the read-only flag.

An API key for one project can list the checks of every other project with the same owner, including uuids and ping URLs with a read-write key, because the list query filters by project owner instead of by the key's project.
A read-only key can obtain a check's uuid, ping URL and management URLs by looking the check up by unique_key, because that view builds the response without passing the read-only flag.
Read-only keys are refused on the channels, pings and ping body endpoints while other read endpoints accept them, blocking a possibly legitimate read path.
A caller can supply the API key in the JSON request body instead of the header.
A key could pass an endpoint it should not, or be matched incorrectly, through the plain-text and hashed key lookup and comparison.
Two projects sharing the same legacy plain-text key could make the key lookup raise MultipleObjectsReturned, because the api_key column has an index but no uniqueness constraint.
